prompt:
A full-body vertical 2:3 (1024×1536) character card image of an adult woman — the personification of the element Hydrogen (수소) itself — the sovereign of the Hydrogen Nation. A female character who IS the element; her costume, ornaments and colors carry the element’s traits. Both hands are ordinary human hands and hold nothing. Age: about twenty — a fresh young-adult face; no facial lines.

Style: A Japanese anime key visual with a painterly finish: an anime-style character with an elegant adult anime face, large expressive eyes, a small nose and mouth, fine coloured linework and soft cel-to-painted shading with painted highlights in the hair and fabric. Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance. No flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face or plastic 3D-render finish.

Her: a clear, innocent purity; porcelain-pale skin; heart-shaped face; large eyes — wide almond eyes, level outer eye corners; thin arched brows; small button nose; small bow lips; sky-blue eyes; rosy flushed cheeks. slender build; an updo bun with choppy uneven bangs; silver-white hair.

Face proportions: a short midface and a soft, gently rounded jawline with a small soft chin — never a long face or a long, pointed or heavy jaw; any crown or headpiece sits above her hairline and never lengthens her face. Her eyes keep the shape described above at a natural open size — never squeezed into narrow slits.

Her element: airy, pale and luminous, always rising: translucent layers, upward-drifting hair and hems, a faint pale-blue flame (hydrogen burns almost invisibly), star-light and fusion white, water droplets and mist; it is the lightest element, the fuel of stars and half of every drop of water. Palette: pale sky blue, white, silver, a faint violet flame, clear glass.

World and costume: around 1900, an airship harbour: great hydrogen gas envelopes under a mooring mast, brass valves and gauges, an electrolysis laboratory with glass jars and a spectroscope, telegraph wires, dawn haze. COSTUME (steampunk): late-Victorian industrial dress — a high-necked blouse with a waistcoat or a tailored tail coat, leather gloves, a work apron or utility belt with brass fittings, goggles hung at the neck or a small instrument as ornament; below, a short bustle skirt over riding trousers and laced boots; muted palette with the traits above as accents. No armor plates, no cape, no crown unless CONCEPT says she wears one; steam, pipes and gauges in the scene; no modern plastic, no sci-fi. LIGHT: hazy gaslight and a smoky overcast sky, unless TIME & WEATHER says otherwise. HAIR: her hair is worn exactly as SILHOUETTE says — loose, long or cut as named; do not pin it up into a bun or tuck it under goggles or a hat unless SILHOUETTE says an updo.

Outfit silhouette: layered linen with a wide-brimmed hat, a belt of glass specimen jars and vine motifs — a greenhouse botanist's soft shape. Only the overall shape is fixed; design the details freely in the element's materials and palette. This silhouette overrides the overall shape of the costume above.

EXPOSURE (bold): the high collar unbuttoned down to the sternum with natural cleavage, sleeves rolled above the elbow, a short bustle skirt showing the legs above laced boots; the waistcoat stays buttoned at the waist. Nothing slipped off. Intimate areas covered; no corset; keep the costume WORLD describes, material and palette.

Pose: standing confidently, her body turned slightly while her face looks toward the viewer. Expression: one brow raised higher, head tilted, eyes wide and attentive, lips slightly parted.

Composition: vertical 2:3 full-body framing with modest headroom and clear space below the boots — the whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet stays inside the frame, occupying about four-fifths of the image height, with the same camera distance in every world; her hands stay inside the frame. Camera at chest height with natural portrait perspective — no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.

Light: the scene's own light, rendered the way this style renders light and skin.

One figure only, natural hands with five fingers; no text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (H) and atomic number (1) — and those only as part of the scene: engraved, embroidered or glowing on her costume, a banner, a sign or a machine, never as a floating label, corner badge, periodic-table tile, caption or overlay on the picture; no logo or watermark.
